dedupe_keys.name: portland bicycle network active planned and recommended facilities

description: The Portland bicycle network layer is a linear feature class of the citywide bicycle network, including bicycle boulevards, bike lanes, multi-use trails and signed connections. A status field marks each facility as active, planned or recommended for future development, so the same layer gives both the existing network and the city's intended future network. It is published by the City of Portland, Oregon, through its PortlandMaps open data services and the city's ArcGIS open data hub, in the transportation and streets category, and is updated as needed. Coverage: the City of Portland, at street-segment resolution. Access: an ArcGIS REST map service layer, the hub page with the usual download formats and a metadata page. Licence and cost: free to download; the hub metadata leave the licence field empty and state no purpose, so reuse terms should be checked with the city. Caveats: planned and recommended segments are intentions that can change, and the layer does not carry traffic volumes or quality ratings. It supports cycling network analysis, comparing today's and future connectivity and exposure of cycle routes to flooding or heat, and pairs with network-quality tools such as the PeopleForBikes Bicycle Network Analysis and with other city cycling layers such as the Victoria bicycle network record.
